title: Is Email Stressing You Out?
main_content:
Few people would disagree that email makes our lives easier. But email can cause problems.

Answering all those emails and processing all that information can overload the brain, causing stress.

So says the Future Work Center, a business based in London. This company carries out psychological research.

The center’s Richard MacKinnon calls email a double-edged sword. In other words, email can be both good and bad.

Psychologists are concerned about the pressure that workers bring on themselves. Dr. Richard MacKinnon spoke with VOA News on Skype.

He says that the stress does not come from the number of emails you get.

According to the study, there are two very stressful email behaviors. One is leaving email on all day. The other is reading and answering emails early in the day and late at night.

questions.question: What can cause stress?
options: The overload of the brain from processing information
The number of friends on social media
The frequency of receiving text messages
The amount of work done during the day
questions.answer: The overload of the brain from processing information

questions.question: If something is a double-edged sword, what is it like?
options: It has both positive and negative effects
It is only beneficial in certain situations
It is dangerous and should be avoided
questions.answer: It has both positive and negative effects

questions.question: What are the two kinds of stressful behaviors that email users can have?
options: Ignoring emails and replying only once a week
Leaving email on all day and reading them early and late
Using separate email accounts for work and personal use
Organizing emails into folders and unsubscribing regularly
questions.answer: Leaving email on all day and reading them early and late
